subject: math
question:
A student was asked to use mathematical induction to prove the following statement.
[Figure: One half plus one fourth plus one eighth plus ... plus (one half) to the n power equals 1 minus (one half) to the n power.]
for all positive integers n
The beginning of the student’s proof is shown below.
[Figure: Blackboard showing the following: First, show that the statement is true for n equals 1: If n equals 1, (one half) to the 1 power equals 1 minus (one half) to the 1 power, one half equals one half. Next, show that if the statement is true when n is equal to a given positive integer k, then it is also true when n is equal to the next integer, k plus 1: Assume that the statement is true when n = k, so one half plus one fourth plus one eighth plus...plus (one half) to the k power equals 1 minus (one half) to the k power. Show that the statement is also true when n is equal to the next integer, k plus 1.]
Complete the student’s proof by showing that if the statement is true when
[Figure: n equals k]
, then it is also true when
[Figure: n equals k plus 1]
, where k is any positive integer.
answer: Scoring guide — Satisfactory: Proof completed correctly

picture.description: One half plus one fourth plus one eighth plus ... plus (one half) to the n power equals 1 minus (one half) to the n power. | Blackboard showing the following: First, show that the statement is true for n equals 1: If n equals 1, (one half) to the 1 power equals 1 minus (one half) to the 1 power, one half equals one half. Next, show that if the statement is true when n is equal to a given positive integer k, then it is also true when n is equal to the next integer, k plus 1: Assume that the statement is true when n = k, so one half plus one fourth plus one eighth plus...plus (one half) to the k power equals 1 minus (one half) to the k power. Show that the statement is also true when n is equal to the next integer, k plus 1. | n equals k | n equals k plus 1
